podcast.title: Layne Staley's Pre-Alice in Chains Band
podcast.body: Sleeze was a glam group where Layne Staley played drums before he was drafted into the band that would eventually become Alice in Chains. Sleeze was later renamed Alice in Chains. "He was drafted in early from another band, a glam group called Sleeze, for whom he played drums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Groups That Changed Their Front-Person and Survived

xref.title: "Kings of Sleeze" Self-Description
xref.body: The Mentors, an extreme punk band from Los Angeles, proudly referred to themselves as the "Kings of Sleeze," a moniker that reflected their provocative and controversial image. This self-proclaimed title was frequently associated with their frontman, Elden Hoke (Eldu-Cher). "They proudly refer to themselves as the Kings of Sleeves."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation and Name Origin
xref.body: Layne Staley had been living with a homeless Jerry Cantrell at their rehearsal space when Sleeze, Staley's band, was eventually renamed Alice in Chains. After Staley's other band (a funk outfit) and Cantrell's separate project both broke up, Cantrell and Sean Kinney asked Staley to be the vocalist for their new group, adopting the name of Staley's former band, Alice in Chains, for the new project. "Sleeze was eventually renamed Alice in Chains, while Lane was living with a homeless Jerry Cantrell at their rehearsal space."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Founding Members and Early Lineup
xref.body: Guitarist Jerry Cantrell and drummer Sean Kinney were the founders of Alice in Chains. Layne Staley was not a founder; he was drafted in early from a glam band called Sleeze, for whom he played drums. "That was guitarist Jerry Cantrell and drummer Sean Kinney. But he was drafted in early from another band, a glam group called Sleeze, for whom he played drums."
